in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== History ==
Its founding period is unknown. It is regarded as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, though there is also a theory that the subordinate shrine Tateiwa Shrine, which manages it as a {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}}, is the actual corresponding shrine.

It is said that a copper {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=tatara}} once stood in this area. In addition, {{ill|Yayoi pottery|es|Cerámica Yayoi|fr|Poterie Yayoi|ja|弥生土器|sl|Jajojsko lončarstvo|sr|Јајои керамика|uk|Кераміка Яйой|qid=Q11487461}} and metal implements have been excavated nearby. It was also called '''Koisha''' (こひしゃ) and '''Kanaya Gongen'''. Another name is '''Kanayama Shrine'''. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was an unranked shrine.

== Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kanayamahiko-no-Kami}}
